title: Branching and Looping
body:
Control flow, once there is no `if` and no `while`. Every structured construct you know
compiles down to two things: change the program counter, or change it conditionally based on
the [[Status Bits]].

## The instructions

| Instruction | Does |
|---|---|
| `bra label` | branch always, unconditional |
| `bcc label` | branch if condition `cc` holds (see below) |
| `jmp label` | jump always, full 32-bit address rather than a relative offset |
| `dbcc dn,label` | decrement-and-branch, the loop instruction |

`bra` is PC-relative and limited in range; `jmp` is absolute and unlimited. Use `bra` unless
the target is far away or computed.

## The conditions

They read the [[Status Bits]] set by whatever ran last, usually a `cmp` or a `tst`. Pick the
family that matches how you are reading the numbers:

| Test | Signed | Unsigned |
|---|---|---|
| equal / not equal | `beq` / `bne` | same |
| greater than | `bgt` | `bhi` |
| greater or equal | `bge` | `bcc` (a.k.a. `bhs`) |
| less than | `blt` | `bcs` (a.k.a. `blo`) |
| less or equal | `ble` | `bls` |

Using a signed branch on unsigned data is a real and quiet bug: `$FF` is greater than `$01`
unsigned and less than it signed, and both branches assemble fine.

Remember `cmp.w d1,d0` computes `d0 - d1`, so `bgt` after it means "d0 > d1". The operand
order looks backwards the first few times.

## Building the structured constructs

**if / else**: branch on the *opposite* of the condition, so the fall-through is the
then-branch.

```
        cmp.w   #10,d0
        blt     else            ; if (d0 >= 10)
        ; then part
        bra     endif
else:   ; else part
endif:
```

**while**: test at the top, branch out; jump back at the bottom.

```
while:  tst.w   d0
        beq     endwhile        ; while (d0 != 0)
        ; body
        bra     while
endwhile:
```

**counted loop with `dbra`**: the idiomatic 68000 loop, and the one that catches people out.
`dbra` (the unconditional form of `dbcc`) decrements the counter and branches while it is
**not −1**, so a loop that should run $n$ times is initialised with $n-1$.

```
        move.w  #10-1,d1        ; ten iterations, note the -1
loop:   ; body
        dbra    d1,loop
```

It only tests the low word of the register, and it exits with the counter at −1, not 0.
